Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Global Asset Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions for joining the question and answer session are available by pressing the * key followed by 1 on your telephone keypad. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Global Asset Management's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Patel, Head of Distribution; Robert Kline, Head of Operations; Elena Vasquez, Head of Risk Management; and David Leung, Head of Technology.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust organic net inflows, favorable market appreciation across equities and fixed income, and strategic execution in high-growth areas like alternatives and ESG strategies. Our AUM grew to $1.45 trillion, reflecting 12% year-over-year expansion and marking our 11th straight quarter of positive organic growth.

This growth was powered by a mix of $28 billion in quarterly net inflows—our strongest since late 2021—plus $45 billion from market gains, particularly in U.S. large-cap equities amid the AI rally, and a small FX tailwind. North America remains our anchor at 55% of AUM or $797.5 billion, up 14% year-over-year on retirement flows and ETF demand. Europe hit $406 billion, up 10%, with ESG bonds thriving post-ECB cuts. Asia-Pacific surged 25% to $174 billion, led by sovereign wealth allocations, while the rest of world added $72.5 billion. Equities drove 45% of inflows, alternatives 10%, positioning us for sustained compounding in a $120 trillion industry.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Johnathan. From a financial perspective, Apex Global Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $875 million to $925 million as guided, representing a 7% to 12% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by management fee revenue of $1.42 billion, up 12% year-over-year, fueled by AUM expansion and resilient average fee rates. Our blended average fee rate stood at 44.8 basis points, down modestly 20 bps year-over-year but stable sequentially, mitigated by shifts toward higher-fee alternatives at 95 bps and institutional mandates.

Expenses were controlled at $610 million to $640 million for the quarter, resulting in net income that keeps our operating margins at 26-28%. Our expense ratio improved to 42 basis points, down 8 bps year-over-year, our 11th straight quarter of compression as AUM outpaced costs 3-to-1. ETFs tightened to 19 bps on scale like our $85 billion S&P 500 tracker, active equities to 68 bps, and alternatives to 112 bps via synergies. For full-year FY24, we guide revenue to $3.55 billion to $3.70 billion, expenses to $2.50 billion to $2.60 billion, assuming $110 billion to $130 billion in net inflows and year-end AUM of $1.38 trillion to $1.45 trillion.

On M&A, we closed two tuck-ins adding $28 billion in AUM at 8.5x revenue multiples—Horizon Sustainable Partners for $12.4 billion in ESG UCITS, enhancing Europe, and Asia Pacific Value Partners for $15.6 billion in ASEAN equities, bolstering APAC. We also announced a 51% stake in Vertex Alternatives' $10 billion private credit platform. These are accretive, with $80 million in synergies, targeting 20-25% of 2025 growth from inorganic sources.

Market performance added $68 billion to AUM, with equities capturing 92% of benchmarks—our U.S. large-cap up 6.1% versus S&P 5.3% on semis overweight. Fixed income gained modestly, alternatives steady at 2.1%. Net flows of $28 billion spanned ETFs ($18 billion), active ($4 billion), and privates ($5 billion), diverse across retail, institutional, and regions—Americas $20 billion, APAC $5 billion.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and alternatives. We're navigating the current market environment by overweighting AI infrastructure, extending duration tactically post-Fed cuts, and scaling privates amid bank retrenchment.

We launched three new products this quarter: the Apex Private Credit Opportunities Fund, a semi-liquid interval fund with $750 million initial AUM targeting 10-12% net IRR via our $2.5 billion origination platform; the Apex Climate Transition ETF (ACTR), gathering $450 million with +18% inception returns using climate risk scoring; and the Apex Asia ex-Japan Growth Fund, seeding €300 million for UCITS distribution. These align with our innovation flywheel, accelerating time-to-market 30%.

Performance rankings shine: 68% of equity funds at 4- or 5-star Morningstar, up from 62%, with flagship Apex Global Equity Fund (AGEFX) 5-star across periods—22.4% 1-year versus MSCI World 19.2%. Core Bond Fund hit 5-stars at 5.6% versus 4.1%, ESG funds 85% Medalist with #1 risk-adjusted returns. We've captured $4.2 billion flows to stars, outranking peers in most categories.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF and multi-asset funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in North America, Europe, and Asia are paying off, as evidenced by partnerships driving 62% of $7.8 billion net inflows, lifting partnership AUM to $182 billion, up 27% year-over-year.

Platform integrations like Envestnet TAM generated $2.1 billion flows via SMA sleeves with 150 bps outperformance; BlackRock Aladdin embedded ESG fixed income for $850 million. Alliances include Vanguard white-labeling our sustainable equity at $1.4 billion YTD and UBS co-branded alternatives at $650 million. Digital pilots with Robinhood seeded $300 million in ETFs, Empower Retirement added $1.2 billion in target-dates. Regionally, North America 68% of flows, Europe 22% via UCITS ETFs, APAC 45% with DBS/HSBC, LatAm $450 million. Tech like Apex FlowHub enables direct indexing and T+0 settlement, guiding $30-35 billion FY24 partnership flows.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've made significant progress in streamlining our middle and back office functions. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk, with straight-through processing at 98% via cloud migrations and India center expansion saving $40 million annually. Compensation ratio improved to 38%, M&A synergies from EuroPacific adding $25 million. We're also focused on scaling shared services and digital transformation, targeting 5-7% productivity gains for 40 bps expense compression by 2025.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Robert. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility, geopolitical tensions, and regulatory shifts like MiFID II and SFDR, and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes stress-testing alternatives for J-curve risks, bolstering ESG exclusions, and integrating climate analytics, ensuring 1.2 Sharpe ratios and 95% retention amid election volatility.

David Leung: Thank you, Elena. On the technology front, we are investing in advanced analytics and AI to enhance our investment decision-making process and improve client service. We are also focused on strengthening our cybersecurity posture. Specifically, our $150 million ApexOne platform—cloud-native on AWS—automates 65% reconciliations, powers NLP sentiment for equities, and enables dynamic fee tiering on $500 billion SMAs. API marketplaces connect 50+ platforms, blockchain betas cut settlements to T+0, and AI personalization reduces churn 15%, scaling robo-advisory to $15 billion AUM.

Johnathan Hale: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes guiding 12-15% organic AUM growth, stabilizing fees at 45 bps via alternatives to 25% mix, launching semi-transparent ETFs, and M&A for ROIC above 18%, all while navigating fee wars and volatility for 5-7% fee revenue CAGR.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Johnson: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the drivers behind your management fee revenue growth and average fee rate trends?

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, Mike. Absolutely. Management fees hit $1.42 billion, up 12% year-over-year on 14% AUM growth to $1.85 trillion, outpacing industry via $85 billion inflows. Blended AFR at 44.8 bps reflects compression offset by alternatives at 95 bps, equities at 65 bps, and institutional stickiness at 38 bps. Americas fees up 15% to $920 million, APAC 22%. ApexOne enables tiering, lifting SMA fees 5 bps; new active ETFs balance passive at 12-25 bps. Q4 guide $1.45-1.50 billion at 44.5 bps.

Mike Johnson: Thank you. And a follow-up on your expense ratio improvements?

Sarah Thompson: Sure. Expense ratio to 42 bps on 3:1 AUM-cost leverage, ETFs at 19 bps, actives 68 bps. Digital transformation automated 65% middle-office, India outsourcing saved $40 million, M&A synergies $25 million. Targeting 40 bps by 2025 via passive shift to 55%, non-fee revenue to 8%. ROE at 22% versus peer 18%.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of your flagship global equity fund?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Emily. AGEFX held 5-star Morningstar across 1-,3-,5-,10-years: 22.4% 1-year vs. 19.2% MSCI World, 11.8% 3-year vs. 9.5%, via 85% active share, AI tilts adding 250 bps. Top 1% Lipper, driving flows.

Emily Chen: And how is the new Climate Transition ETF performing relative to expectations?

Lisa Patel: Exceeding, Emily. ACTR at $450 million AUM, +18% inception vs. +12% clean energy index, using ML on IPCC data. Outpacing peers, 55% North America inflows, resonating in balanced mandates.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan.

David Patel: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Robert Kline: Happy to, David. GAP One on AWS slashed unit costs 15%, India center handles 80% KYC/AML for $40 million savings. Compensation to 38% of revenues, post-M&A rationalization. Gen-AI for 5-7% gains, mirroring leaders.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Gonzalez with Barclays.

Laura Gonzalez: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Elena Vasquez: Thanks, Laura. Robust monitoring of MiFID II, SFDR, CSRD—enhanced ESG scoring avoids 15% carbon-intensive, Paris-Aligned 30% Europe AUM by 2026. Stress-tests for volatility, privates; retention 98%, Sharpe 1.25.

Operator: Our next question comes from Kevin Wong with Citigroup.

Kevin Wong: How are you leveraging technology to improve investment performance?

David Leung: Great question, Kevin. ApexOne integrates MSCI/Refinitiv ESG, NLP for Asia transcripts, climate satellite data—boosted Sharpe 0.2 pre-launch. Fee optimization analyzes 10 million interactions, robo at $15 billion with 12 bps costs, blockchain for T+0.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Global Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
